clue.text: Measure in force for trade

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: coerce means force
mm, millimetre, is a measure of length

explanation.surface: A law is enacted to regulate business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' looks like a law or policy, but it is the unit MM.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is the buying and selling of goods, a synonym.

clue.text: Gracefulness for 7 in oriental weapon

parts.note: E for East, oriental meaning eastern

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a lance is a weapon
the answer to clue 7 means 'for example', abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: Grace of movement is shown in an eastern weapon display.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' refers to 7-down, whose definition is 'for example', giving EG; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance means refined grace and style in movement or appearance.

clue.text: Figures test sound points of view

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: try means test
angles are viewpoints or perspectives

explanation.surface: Numbers put opinions to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reasonable, but it signals that TRY is heard as TRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-sided shapes are geometric figures.

clue.text: Awful spite due to understudy

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reluctantly takes over a role, bitter at having to stand in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges SPITE and DUE together; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To understudy is to stand in for someone else, which is what a substitute does.

clue.text: Brain disorder may be Times murder line

indicators.note: may be says these letters could become another word once rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a killing could cause a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges TIMES MURDER LINE together; Times is the newspaper that printed the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: This alcohol withdrawal condition brings on tremors and hallucinations affecting the mind.

clue.text: Ineffective exhortation to economise

explanation.surface: Advice to save money that does no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: worthless and of no practical help, and read as two words, an urging to consume a smaller amount.

clue.text: Sophisticated attitude, for example

parts.note: in means fashionable, in vogue, akin to sophisticated
a stance is an attitude or position

explanation.surface: A worldly outlook is offered as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: IN as 'fashionable' stretches to 'sophisticated' in old Times usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'for instance' means for example, so this noun is an example or case.

clue.text: Biblical stone chapel

explanation.surface: An Old Testament monument and a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the stone Samuel set up to commemorate help from God, and a common name for Nonconformist chapels in Wales and England.

clue.text: The swelling act of the — theme" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: The swelling act of the — theme" (Macbeth)

parts.words: The swelling act of the — theme" (Macbeth)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Macbeth's aside after the witches' prophecy: the missing word describes a theme of kingship and empire

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is Macbeth's 'happy prologues to the swelling act of the imperial theme', spoken as he dreams of being king.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adjective describes the theme of an emperor's rule, which Macbeth imagines for himself.

clue.text: Not so much freedom, say, for the tenant

indicators.note: say tells us the words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: less means not so much, and ease means freedom from difficulty: 'less ease'

explanation.surface: A renter complains that the lease gives them less freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less ease' spoken quickly gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person holding a property on a lease is the one who rents it from the landlord.

clue.text: Reduced rent for servant

explanation.surface: A landlord lowers the rent for a household worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a reduced fee paid to keep lodgings while away, and a long-serving domestic employee in a household.

clue.text: Changed into insect in the river? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
this swaps the roles, so the insect goes around the river instead of inside it

parts.note: a bee is an insect
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a creature turned into an insect while in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, the insect would go into the river; 'Quite the reverse' swaps that, so the river sits inside the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: If something turned into a new form, it grew or developed into it, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Insensitive, nonetheless, about copper's method of reasoning

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps around another
read as 'none-the-less', meaning the round letter for nothing is removed

parts.note: callous means insensitive, unfeeling
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An unfeeling policeman still has his own way of working things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' says take O (none, zero) away, leaving CALLUS before 'about' wraps it round. 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Calculus, in its older sense, is any system of calculation or formal reasoning.

clue.text: Capital for a peer's cup perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints these letters might form something else when rearranged

parts.note: the word as written including its s

explanation.surface: A trophy cup meant for a member of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A, PEERS and CUP together. 'Capital' looks like a city or money, but means a large letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are also called large letters, from the top type tray in printing.

clue.text: Honour for "Kismet" announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: kismet is fate or destiny

explanation.surface: An award is given for the musical Kismet and publicly declared.
explanation.walkthrough: Kismet is also a musical, which pulls the surface toward theatre awards.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to celebrate or pay tribute to them lavishly.

clue.text: Bird, animal and man measured by volume

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
a rat is an animal
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A bird, a creature and a person are sized up by volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'measured by volume' is chemistry: a titration measures concentration using volumes of solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Titration is a chemical analysis where amounts are found from volumes of liquid added.

clue.text: He can foretell the directions royalty is to follow

indicators.note: is to follow says the royal piece comes after the directions

parts.note: S and E, south and east, are compass directions
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A prophet predicts which way the royal family is heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet or visionary is someone who can predict the future.

clue.text: Sign of derision about one in the river.

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: scorn means derision

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: the Po is the river of northern Italy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mocking gesture made about someone in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside PO to give PIO, and 'about' wraps the scorn round that. 'Sign' looks like a gesture, but means a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: This arachnid is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Questions rising cut at pits

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: axe means cut
mines are pits

explanation.surface: Inquiries are made about cuts in the coal pits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns AXE into EXA; 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone formally is to probe or interrogate them, a synonym.

clue.text: Is love the subject? It's to do with an elementary form

definitions.text: It's to do with an elementary form

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a topic is a subject of discussion

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a piece of writing is about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elementary' means relating to chemical elements: isotopes are forms of one element.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopes are variants of a chemical element with different numbers of neutrons, so this adjective concerns such forms.

clue.text: Establish where the horse's place is

explanation.surface: Setting up the stable for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to set up or put in place, and read as two words, located inside the horse's stable box.

clue.text: Vicar restores part of stall

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clergyman repairs a section of the choir stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stall' looks like a church seat, matching the vicar, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall something is to halt or check it, a synonym.

clue.text: Tympana might make Mars rude

indicators.note: might make says these letters could be formed into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the planet or war god could be made impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tympanum is the anatomical term for the membrane in the ear, and tympana is its plural.

clue.text: Film people in wild sex painting taken aback

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
wild suggests disorder, so these letters are jumbled
taken aback means turned backwards, so this word is written from end to start

parts.note: painting is art

explanation.surface: Actors appear in a racy picture and are shocked by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' makes EXS and 'taken aback' makes TRA; 'in' puts the second inside the first. 'Film people' looks like stars, but means background actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Background actors in crowd scenes are hired to appear in movies, the cinema's supporting people.

clue.text: Like the Mediterranean in season, to a smaller degree

parts.note: tide in its old sense is a season, as in Yuletide or Eastertide
less means to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: The Mediterranean is said to be calmer at certain times of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. TIDE as season survives in Christmastide and Whitsuntide.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean Sea has almost no rise and fall of the sea level, so it barely has tides.

clue.text: Character holding a title role in Wilde play

definitions.text: Character holding a title role in Wilde play

parts.words: Character holding a title role in Wilde play
parts.note: in The Importance of Being Earnest, a character goes by the name punned on in the title, so he holds the title role in a double sense

explanation.surface: A question about who plays the lead in an Oscar Wilde comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Worthing calls himself by this name, which sounds like the title's adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's farce turns on a man using this false name, the title's pun on being serious.
